decision: Dropped the 45 exact repeat rows with drop_duplicates(keep='first'), leaving 30000 patients.
reason: An identical row is the same registration entered twice, so keeping one copy makes patient_id unique without losing information.

issue: gender spellings that are not a code
decision: Stripped and lowercased gender, mapped female/woman/f to F, male/man/m to M, and nonbinary/non-binary/nb/x to X with Series.map(), set unknown and blanks to missing, and stored it as a category.
reason: The 6968 non-code spellings and 486 blanks all carry one of three meanings or none, and the data dictionary allows only F, M, X, or missing.

decision: Uppercased site_code and removed every hyphen and space, so the 1811 variants such as n-01 become N01, S02, or E04.
reason: The variants are typing differences for the same three registry sites, and normalized codes are needed to join patients to sites.

decision: Converted birth_year to Int64 and replaced the 371 values of 9999 with missing.
reason: 9999 means not recorded, so leaving it as a number would distort ages and the birth_year min and max.

issue: weight column named wt_kg in visits_south.csv
decision: Renamed wt_kg to weight_kg in a copy of visits_south before stacking it under visits_north.
reason: Both files record the same measurement, so one column name lets the 31074 south rows stack into weight_kg instead of a mostly empty extra column.

issue: sbp sentinel 999 and readings outside 70 through 250
decision: Converted sbp_mmhg to numbers, kept 70 through 250 inclusive as Int64, and set the 341 values of 999 and the 116 out-of-range values to missing.
reason: 999 means not measured and readings outside 70 to 250 mmHg are not plausible clinic values, while 70 and 250 themselves are valid boundary readings.

issue: impossible and loosely written visit dates
decision: Kept visit_date only when the text is exact YYYY-MM-DD and parses to a real calendar date, setting the 169 others to missing.
reason: Loose formats are ambiguous and impossible dates such as 2026-02-30 cannot be real visits, so guessing would plant wrong dates.

decision: After removing exact repeats, showed the 120 pairs measured twice and kept the later reading by visit_time with drop_duplicates(keep='last').
reason: A same-day recheck replaces the first reading, and keeping one row per patient and visit is what the pivot and the joins require.

decision: Kept only rows whose record_status is current, so N01 and S02 each keep one name and the retired versions are dropped.
reason: N01 and S02 each have a current and a retired record, and only one row per site_code lets the visit-to-site join stay many-to-one.
